title: Token ladder + retainer hybrid — quickmaths and heuristics
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad for a hybrid pricing idea — small retainer (seat or fixed fee) + per-token ladder pricing that decays as committed monthly usage increases. Useful as a starter for GTM + sales enablement notes.

Big picture summary (one-liner):
- Small monthly retainer buys SLO-backed capacity and a baseline token allotment; overage is billed with volume-discount ladders and optional latency/SLO premiums.

Key heuristics and assumptions (back-of-envelope):
- Baseline infra economics: assume amortized GPU-hour cost to token = 0.02 USD per 1k tokens at 8k context average (includes infra, power, infra ops). (See later calc.)
- Margin target for hosted API SKU = 60% gross on token revenue (post infra).
- Sales/discount reserve and support: 15% of revenue on average across small customers (assume).
- Customer behaviour buckets: low (<=10M tokens/mo), mid (10M–200M), high (>200M).

Retainer sizing ideas:
- Micro-retainer (SMB): $50–200/mo — covers 100k–1M baseline tokens and SLO 95th latency guardrails.
- Team-retainer (SMB+): $500–2k/mo — covers 1M–15M baseline tokens, priority support, small dedicated burst pool.
- Enterprise down-payment: committable credits (prepay) that also buy Dedicated routing/priority and a guaranteed min throughput.

Token ladder (example) — price per 1k tokens (hosted API):
- up to 5M/mo: $0.065 / 1k tokens
- 5M–50M: $0.045 / 1k tokens
- 50M–250M: $0.025 / 1k tokens
- >250M: $0.012 / 1k tokens (or customdedicated pricing)

Hybrid retainer mechanics (early design):
- Retainer covers X tokens (X depends on tier) at a deeply discounted effective rate (e.g., equates to 25–40% off list) because it also pre-pays SLO capacity.
- Overages charged per-ladder above. Retainer gets rollover credits up to 30 days to avoid angry churn.
- If customer opts for canary/dedicated routing, apply surcharge or require committed tier.

Example scenarios (quick math):
1) Micro SAAS: retainer $150/mo covers 1M tokens. They use 3M tokens/mo. Billing: retainer covers 1M (effective rate = $0.15 / 1k), remaining 2M billed at first ladder ($0.065). Total = $150 + (2,000 * $0.065) = $150 + $130 = $280/mo. Effective blended rate = ~$0.093 / 1k tokens.

2) Scale app (mid): retainer $1,200/mo covers 6M tokens. Monthly usage 60M. Overages: first 44M at $0.045, next 10M at $0.025 (simplified). Compute: retainer $1,200 + (44,000 * 0.045) + (10,000 * 0.025) = $1,200 + $1,980 + $250 = $3,430 => blended ~$0.057 / 1k. Note we might add a latency premium if 95th > threshold.

Amortized GPU-hour -> token rough derivation:
- Typical T4/RTX A10x cost per GPU-hour on infra (spot-like amortized with ops) = ~$2.50–$6 (varies). Use $4/h as middle.
- Throughput roughness: model at 8k context, continuous stream, avg 500 tokens/sec on a 4 GPU pod (?) — this is fuzzy; better to use token/sec per GPU ~= 150–400 depending on model/quant. Take conservative 200 tokens/sec => 720k tokens/hour per GPU.
- Cost per 1k tokens = ($4 / 720k) * 1000 = ~$0.0056 per 1k tokens. Add ops/cooling/network + multiple replicas + batching inefficiencies => x3 => ~$0.017 per 1k tokens. Aligns with earlier ~0.02 assumption.
- Sensitivity: if token/sec halves, cost doubles. If quantized models + batching increase throughput by 2x, cost halves.

Service-level adjustments / premiums idea:
- Latency premium: +20% on per-token price if customer requires p95 < 100ms at 90% traffic (meaning lower batching, more nodes).
- SLO-backed minimum commit: customers with SLA require minimum monthly commit (e.g., $5k/mo) or pay an extra 10% surcharge on per-token rates.
- Burst capacity: optional burst pool (retainer or add-on) priced as $/peak-GPU-hour equivalent; useful for apps with spiky conversational flows.

Sales-discount banding and negotiation levers (how sales can discount while protecting economics):
- Reduce effective per-1k price by increasing retainer (shift revenue from variable to committed).
- Increase minimum term (12/24 months) for deeper discounts — amortize onboarding and SW/hard costs.
- Offer overage smoothing (cap step-downs) but tie to data sharing/usage analytics.

Edge cases and open questions to resolve: 
- Rollover design: how many days? Impacts revenue recognition and churn behavior. Recommended 30 days for SMB, none for enterprise.
- Fractional seat amortization: when retainer includes seat + baseline compute, how to split for accounting? (needed for quoting.)
- Metering for function-calls vs. streaming tokens: sessionization and small-control tokens can blow counts. Need heuristics to discount control tokens or meter conversational sessions differently.
- Fairness for KV cache heavy users (few tokens per request but high compute due to retrievals). Consider quoting on compute-equivalent or add a per-call compute surcharge.

Next steps / TODOs (personal):
- Model 12 sample customer profiles (0.5M, 2M, 15M, 40M, 120M, 500M tokens) and run sensitivity for infra cost +/-50%.
- Sync with pricing-data (finance) — ask Raj for historical infra per-GPU-hour amortization and SRE ops cost buckets.
- Draft short cheat-sheet for AE playbook: \"How to shift customers to higher retainer to unlock discounts\".
- Put a tiny prototype calculator in a shared sheet and link from Confluence page.

Notes-to-self: reference old spreadsheets under /shared_drives/go-to-market/pricing/ but keep this user's scratchpad for early ideas. Keep the ladders intentionally simple for first pass — avoid >4 bands until we have telemetry.

Slack/context links:
- Pricing channel thread: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/CPRICING/p159753 (quick sketch from Priya that inspired retainer idea)
- JIRA ticket for hybrid pilot: JIRA-ENG-1932 (needs SRE scope)

Rough sales messaging snippets (for AE use):
- \"Start small, guarantee latency — add a tiny retainer and get a predictable token budget each month. Grow with volume discounts that kick in automatically.\"
- \"Commit to a small monthly minimum and lock in lower unit economics — you pay less per token as your usage grows, and we reserve capacity to keep your tail latencies low.\"

End of scratchpad. Will formalize after sprint planning and data from infra/finance.
